title: Kant suppressed Swedenborg's disturbing accounts

tellings.quote: Kant admits that the reason that he did this is that the stuff in Swedenborg is so disturbing that it would destabilize society, including on a political level.

plain: The philosopher Jason Jorjani says that the German philosopher Immanuel Kant, who lived in Königsberg, Prussia, deliberately pushed aside the writings of Emanuel Swedenborg, a mystic who wrote about the spirit world in books such as Arcana Coelestia (Secrets of Heaven). According to Jorjani, Kant admitted he did this because Swedenborg's material was "so disturbing that it would destabilize society, including on a political level". Jorjani gives this as his own summary without naming a source, though he links it to Kant's book Groundwork of the Metaphysics of Morals and to his own book Prometheus and Atlas.
